---
title: "US Designations"
subtitle: "Every tracked Chinese semiconductor entity under US export-control designations"
description: "Sortable table of all facilities, design firms, and equipment/materials firms on the Commerce/BIS Entity List or DoD Section 1260H list, with dates and sources."
date: last-modified
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
source("R/helpers.R")
library(DT)

desig <- load_designations()
n_entity  <- sum(desig$kind == "Facility")
n_design  <- sum(desig$kind == "Design firm")
n_mat     <- sum(desig$kind == "Equipment & materials")
n_fn4     <- sum(grepl("FN4", desig$designation))
n_1260h   <- sum(desig$designation == "DoD 1260H")
```

## Why this page exists

"Entity List" and "Chinese Military Companies list" are used interchangeably in
public debate, but they are **legally distinct instruments with distinct
consequences**:

- **Entity List (Commerce/BIS)** — an export-control denial order. US and many
  non-US suppliers need BIS licences (presumed deniable) to sell items subject
  to the EAR to the listed party. This is the list that stops a fab from buying
  lithography. Entries marked **FN4** additionally carry Footnote 4: the Foreign
  Direct Product Rule reaches *foreign-made* chips designed for the listed
  firm — the tool that caught SMIC's 7nm effort and the two GPU startups.
- **Section 1260H (Defense/DoD)** — a transparency designation of
  "Chinese military companies." It bans DoD procurement contracts and channels
  reputational pressure, but it does **not** by itself restrict trade in chips
  or tools. Firms can sit on one list, the other, or both; this tracker records
  which, exactly, for each entry.

This page lists every designated entity in the tracker, kept distinct, so the
difference between *blocked from buying tools* and *named as a military company*
never gets lost in a headline. A "no designation" entry in the trackers is not
a claim that the firm is clean — only that no designation is currently on
record.

## The register

```{r table, echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
table_data <- desig %>%
  mutate(
    Name = paste0('<a href="', page, '">', name, '</a>'),
    Designation = factor(designation, levels = c("Entity List (BIS)", "Entity List · FN4", "DoD 1260H")),
    Kind = factor(kind),
    Added = format(date, "%d %b %Y"),
    Detail = gsub("US Commerce BIS", "BIS", gsub("US DoD ", "", list_raw))
  ) %>%
  select(Name, Designation, Kind, Added, Sector = sub, Location = place, Detail)

datatable(
  table_data,
  escape = FALSE,
  filter = list(position = "top", clear = TRUE),
  options = list(
    pageLength = 25, dom = "ftip", scrollX = TRUE,
    order = list(list(3, "desc")),
    columnDefs = list(list(className = "dt-right", targets = 3))
  ),
  rownames = FALSE
)
```

**`r nrow(desig)`** entities are designated: **`r n_entity`** facilities, **`r n_design`** design firms, **`r n_mat`** equipment/materials firms — including **`r n_fn4`** Footnote-4 (FDPR) entries and **`r n_1260h`** on the DoD 1260H list. Dates are the designation date on record in the tracker's data; the underlying citations sit on each entity's profile page.

::: {.callout-note}
## How to read the FN4 column value
Footnote 4 attaches to an entity, but its bite falls on whoever *manufactures
for* that entity — which is why SMIC itself sits on the plain Entity List while
Biren and Moore Threads, the designers it cannot openly serve, carry FN4.
:::
